## Body

Security review of PR #298, round 1.

Head: 12bdede47db345264785d667f50ced08ef85e8dc
Base: 44f313e4954f50584a278ef7907d442de32ddc67

Verdict: BLOCK. Keep F241 APPLY held. These findings concern incorrect absence evidence at destructive/lifecycle safety boundaries, not isolation from hostile same-user seats (C33).

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| S298-001 | 🟠 HIGH | justfile | 795-799 | Textual socket comparison fails open for macOS /tmp versus /private/tmp aliases. | 10/10 |
| S298-002 | 🟠 HIGH | crates/testkit/src/tmux_sweep.rs | 219-224, 247-253, 304-309 | Lossy path parsing and silently discarded metadata failures classify live sockets as absent. | 10/10 |

S298-001: On the refusal path, tmux preserves the socket spelling supplied through TMUX, whereas lsof can report its physical spelling. A native macOS probe confirmed that the /tmp and /private/tmp spellings have the same device/inode, but only the physical spelling matches the lsof output. The exact-head extracted bounce guard reports "allowed" for that mismatch. Thus a live backlogged server can still be treated as absent and the daemon signalled without _pij protection. The correctness reviewer independently reproduced the normal-use alias case. Resolve identity rather than comparing raw display strings; any unresolved identity must refuse.

S298-002: Native /usr/sbin/lsof -nP -a -U -u <uid> -F n returned exit 0 while rendering newline, backslash and tab characters as escaped text. The new parser does not decode that representation. Holders::read then silently drops fs::metadata failures and returns Known without those listeners. Normal and space-containing names were recognized; all three escaped names were missed. The correctness reviewer compiled the sweep module copied from the frozen head into a scratch proof crate, with only UID/O_NOFOLLOW/constants stubs. Its native macOS test classified and removed all three live sockets; the space case remained Live. Separately, a replay of the exact Linux nth(7) parser truncated a space-bearing TMUX_TMPDIR path and removed one live socket. That is a Linux parser replay on macOS, not a native Linux runtime result. Both tests failed their expected-Live assertions (exit 101). A prior cached-binary run corroborated the macOS result but is not used as exact-head build proof. Preserve uncertainty instead of silently turning an unresolvable holder path into absence.

Additional boundedness observation: justfile:796 invokes PATH-resolved lsof without an internal deadline. A hanging fake lsof kept the extracted guard waiting until the probe killed its own process group. This remains fail-closed with respect to signalling, but can stall bounce indefinitely. It is not a separate destructive fail-open block.

Policy versus brake: the sweep's destructive policy is absence of a holder; lossy or unresolvable paths do not establish that absence. Its young-file grace remains a brake (removing it can only delete more). The fixture's destructive policy is positive server-PID exit. The bounce holder check is a brake, but the alias mismatch incorrectly releases it.

Validation receipts:

- just pr-freeze 298: FINAL at the full head above; main base, CLEAN, not draft, all five latest CI jobs passed, no migration changes, Delivers accepted.
- Native macOS socket/lsof probe, run using nice -n 19 python3 -: exit 0; normal and space names held=True; newline, backslash and tab names held=False; tmp_alias_same_inode=True; alias text match=False, physical text match=True.
- Exact-head source-extracted bounce-guard probe, nice -n 19 python3 -: exit 0. Exact match blocked; suffix allowed; spaces/metacharacters handled literally; nonzero, permission exit, and partial output with a failing exit blocked. Three mutations were caught: force-unheld, nonzero fail-open, and substring matching. A successful truncated record was accepted as unheld; no claim is made that arbitrary exit-zero truncation can be detected.
- Refusal-string audit: rg --hidden -n 'ECONNREFUSED|ConnectionRefused|no server running' crates/daemon crates/tmux returned only crates/daemon/src/serve.rs:94. Inspected serve.rs:48-62,91-98: it classifies TCP accept errors for retry, not server absence or deletion. No additional refusal-as-gone path was found by this audit.
- Fixture probe: #{pid} identified the tmux server, not the pane process; live kill(pid,0) succeeded. PID reuse is conservatively retained, not used to authorize deletion.
- Exact-head source-extracted shared-build pre-cargo prefix probe, nice -n 19 python3 -: exit 0. Failed stamp creation removed the stale stamp and released the lock. An unwritable target returned 7 before the cargo boundary, retained the stamp bytes, and released the lock. Removing either the exit-7 guard or stale-stamp removal was caught. No cargo was invoked by this probe.
- Independent correctness-review receipt: just shared-build --timeout 180s -- test --offline --manifest-path <owned-proof-root>/review298-path-probes/Cargo.toml reviewer_path_checks -- --nocapture returned 101 with two expected-Live regressions RED: reviewer_live_lsof_names_must_not_look_absent (removed 3), reviewer_linux_parser_preserves_space_in_tmpdir (removed 1). The absolute proof-root path is intentionally redacted for public publication. The retained result.log/result.json are under review298-path-probes in that reviewer's session artifacts.
- Cached Rust timeout/unknown-holder tests passed, but are not claimed as exact-head build proof.
- harness boot --json: advisory ready=false because vitest is absent. No dependencies were installed or symlinked (C25); TypeScript proof remains exact-head CI.
- harness checks --json: attempted, then stopped to release the shared cargo target for the correctness reviewer's focused tests. No completed local full-gate verdict is claimed.

All destructive probes were confined to owned scratch directories. No product files were edited and no production sweep was applied. No live daemon performance certification is claimed by this security verdict.

Other boundaries: no new secret, credential or non-pij home-path disclosure was identified in the changed files. Sweep candidate checks retain symlink_metadata (tmux_sweep.rs:313,340,349); the new holder lookup uses metadata to resolve identities, not to follow a candidate during removal. Bounce argument/match quoting handled literal spaces and shell metacharacters in the probe. Its lsof executable is PATH-resolved, not absolute; under C33 this is not a hostile-local-process finding.

Static cost scope: one absolute-path lsof per manual macOS sweep with a 10-second child deadline, no per-entry launch; fixture kill(pid,0) every 10 ms for at most 2 seconds, no launch for those polls; one lsof on the bounce refusal path, but no internal deadline there. No recurring daemon loop was added. Fleet before/after performance acceptance belongs to the performance verdict, not this security receipt.

Harness feedback: the existing dependency-free review-readiness gap remains. A review scope that reports exact-head CI and dependency-free probes without prescribing shared dependency links or duplicating a locked full cargo gate would prevent this run's setup and build contention. Captured observations remain in the review's per-agent harness buffer.
